title: Implement HERC device model under local equilibrium approximation
action: Implement the heat-recovery solar cell model using the local equilibrium approximation. Define Si absorber parameters (band gap 1.12 eV, effective masses, thickness 100 μm), the solar spectrum (AM0 approximated by 6000 K blackbody radiation at 1 sun concentration), and the coupled equations for charge balance (Eq. 48), extraction current (Eq. 43, including the ohmic voltage drop term dV_ohmic and heat balance (Eq. 58)). Incorporate thermal contact resistance via effective length l_eff scaling. Use the optimal barrier heights and extraction times provided for each absorber temperature (350 K: E_b=0.39 eV, τ_out=1e-7 s; 400 K: E_b=0.47 eV, τ_out=3e-7 s; 450 K: E_b=0.55 eV, τ_out=3e-6 s). The code must find the maximum power point while enforcing the heat-supply condition (P_Qin + P_T > 0) for stable operation.
description: Required intermediate: write the simulation code that will be used by the downstream scored steps.

title: Compute efficiency vs absorber temperature and κ/σ
action: For each combination of T_ph in {350, 400, 450} K and κ/σ in {0, 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2.5} V^2/K, run the implemented device model to obtain the maximum power conversion efficiency η_max (in %). Enforce the heat-supply condition P_Qin+P_T>0. Write the results to a CSV file with columns: T_ph (K), kappa_sigma (V^2/K), eta_max (%).
description: Main scored artifact: efficiency as a function of operating temperature and filtering-layer conductivity ratio. The verifier will compare values to hidden gold with tolerance and perform structural checks (non‑increasing with κ/σ, positive slope for κ/σ=0, negative slope for κ/σ≥1e-2.5).
output_schema: Columns: T_ph (K), kappa_sigma (V^2/K), eta_max (%). Each row corresponds to one (T_ph, kappa_sigma) combination.

title: Derive analytic bound on κ/σ
action: Using the optimal barrier height E_b = 0.55 eV (for T_ph = 450 K) and the elementary charge q, compute the upper bound κ/σ ≤ (E_b/q) × 3.0×10⁻³ V²/K. Write two lines: first line the literal inequality 'kappa/sigma <= (Eb/q) * 3.0e-3 V^2/K', second line the numerical value of the bound in V^2/K.
description: Scored deterministic calculation of the material requirement. Verifier checks the numeric value against the exact result within tolerance and the text format.
output_schema: Line 1: 'kappa/sigma <= (Eb/q) * 3.0e-3 V^2/K'. Line 2: numerical bound in V^2/K (e.g., 1.65e-3).

title: Evaluate candidate materials against bound
action: Using reported material properties: for Bi₂Te₃, σ ≈ 1×10⁵ S/m and κ ≈ 1.4 W/(m·K); for CsSnI₃, σ ≈ 3×10⁴ S/m and κ ≈ 0.6 W/(m·K). Compute κ/σ for each and determine whether the material satisfies the analytic bound derived in the previous step. Write two lines, one per material, in the format '<Material>: kappa/sigma = <value> V^2/K, <comment>'.
description: Scored verification that the reported materials satisfy the bound. Verifier extracts the computed κ/σ values and compares them to the exact numbers within tolerance, and checks the full string content.
output_schema: Line 1: 'Bi2Te3: kappa/sigma = X.XXe-X V^2/K, satisfies bound but band gap too small.' Line 2: 'CsSnI3: kappa/sigma = Y.YYe-Y V^2/K, satisfies bound with usable band gap.'
